title: Is Carpet Bad for Allergies? What the Research Actually Says
meta: Carpet is not bad for allergies by itself. Research shows it traps allergens if vacuumed weekly with HEPA vacuum. Wills Flooring on carpet in Snohomish homes.
keywords: is carpet bad for allergies, carpet and asthma research, best carpet for allergy sufferers, carpet vs hardwood for allergies, dust mites in carpet, carpet installation Snohomish WA

blocks.lead: Not by itself. The research does not show that carpet causes allergies or asthma; it shows that carpet holds dust, dander and mite allergen in the pile, which is a problem if you never remove it and an advantage if you vacuum it out weekly with a HEPA machine.
blocks.detail: Hard floors let the same allergens stay airborne and recirculate until they settle. The honest answer depends on how you clean, how damp the house is, and who in the family is allergic to what. Snohomish homes add mud, dogs, wood smoke and crawlspace moisture to the equation.

blocks.html: A common Reddit thread asks whether ripping out carpet cured someone's allergies, and the replies split evenly between yes, no and it was the cat. That matches the science, which is messier than either side admits. Around Snohomish the question has a local flavor: acreage that tracks in mud and grass pollen, dogs on the bedroom floor, a wood stove putting fine ash into the air all winter, and a vented crawlspace under a farmhouse near Blackmans Lake keeping the floor damp enough for mites. Here is what the studies found and where carpet belongs in an allergic household.

items.title: Airborne dust is often lower in carpeted rooms
items.text: Room-comparison studies have measured fewer fine particles in the air above carpet than above hard floors, because the pile holds dust down instead of letting footsteps kick it up. That holds only while the carpet is cleaned; a neglected one becomes a reservoir that releases allergen with every step.

items.title: Dust mite allergen is higher in carpet
items.text: Mites live in the pile and pad and feed on skin flakes. Studies consistently find more mite allergen in carpet than on bare floors, especially in humid homes. Mites need humidity above about 50 percent, which is why a damp Snohomish crawlspace matters more than the carpet.

items.title: No consistent link to asthma
items.text: Large reviews have not found that living with carpet causes asthma or makes it worse in any consistent way. One often-cited country-level comparison showed asthma rising while carpet sales fell, which proves nothing either way but undercuts the idea that removal is a cure.

items.title: Pet dander goes everywhere
items.text: Dander is small, sticky and airborne. It settles on carpet, but also on couches, bedding and hard floors. Households with a dog measure dander on every surface, so the floor is one part of the picture, not the cause.

blocks.text: Which carpet is best for an allergic household

items.html: Low, dense pile. A short frieze or tight loop holds less dust and gives it up to the vacuum more easily than a deep plush. Shag is the worst choice.

Nylon or triexta, solution-dyed. Synthetic fibers do not feed mites or absorb moisture the way wool can, and solution-dyed yarn takes hot-water extraction without fading. Our fiber comparison goes deeper.

A dense pad with a moisture barrier. Pad is where mites and pet accidents collect. A dense rebond or felt pad with a sealed top layer keeps liquids on the surface so they can be extracted instead of soaking in.
Skip antimicrobial claims. Treatments marketed as allergen-fighting have little evidence behind them. The vacuum and the humidity level do the work, not the label.

blocks.text: The cleaning routine that makes carpet allergy-safe

items.text: HEPA vacuum with a sealed body, slow overlapping passes, twice a week where the dog sleeps. A cheap vacuum without HEPA blows the fine allergen straight back into the air.
Check indoor humidity with a cheap hygrometer. Above 50 percent, run a dehumidifier or look at the crawlspace. Dry air is the most effective mite control there is.
Shoes off, a real outdoor mat and a washable indoor mat. Most pollen and mud in a Snohomish house arrives on boots and paws.
Professional hot-water extraction, then dry the carpet fully within 24 hours with fans. Damp carpet after cleaning is how mold starts, so skip the wettest weeks of winter.
Replace it. Old pad holds decades of allergen no cleaning reaches. When we pull carpet in a 1990s house, the pad is the worst part.

blocks.title: Fix the crawlspace before you blame the carpet:
blocks.text: Many Snohomish homes on Fobes Hill and out toward Clearview sit over vented crawlspaces with standing water in winter. That moisture rises through the subfloor and keeps carpet and pad damp enough for mites and mold no matter how often you vacuum. A vapor barrier and a dehumidifier do more for an allergic family than any flooring change.

faq.a: Sometimes, mainly for people allergic to dust mites in a humid house. For dander and pollen, removal changes little because those settle on every surface. Some families report more sneezing afterward, because dust that was held in the pile is now airborne with every footstep. Vacuuming and humidity control matter more than the surface.

faq.q: Is carpet or hardwood better for asthma?
faq.a: The evidence does not clearly favor either. Carpet holds particles down between cleanings; hard floors let them recirculate but are easier to clean completely. For asthma triggered by dust mites, a hard floor in the bedroom plus a dehumidified house is safer. For most other triggers, a well-vacuumed low-pile carpet is fine.

faq.q: What is the best carpet for allergy sufferers?
faq.a: A low, dense cut pile or tight loop in solution-dyed nylon or triexta, over a dense pad with a moisture barrier, certified Green Label Plus. The short pile releases dust to the vacuum, the synthetic fiber does not hold moisture, and the barrier pad keeps spills and pet accidents from soaking into the cushion where mites live.

faq.q: How often should you vacuum carpet if you have allergies?
faq.a: Once a week minimum with a sealed HEPA vacuum, twice a week in rooms where pets sleep, using slow overlapping passes rather than quick ones. A vacuum without a HEPA filter and a sealed body pushes the smallest particles back into the air, which can make symptoms worse right after cleaning.

faq.q: Do dust mites live in carpet?
faq.a: Yes, in the pile and especially in the pad, wherever there are skin flakes to eat and humidity above about 50 percent. Below that they struggle to survive. In a Snohomish house over a damp crawlspace the fix is a vapor barrier and a dehumidifier; in a dry house, weekly vacuuming keeps them low.
